facts.statement: A sheep herder named Ma Yun discovered the dinosaur bones in 2004.
facts.quote: In 2004, sheep herder Ma Yun found dinosaur bones, notifying local administrators Yang Huozhu and Liu Hongan.

facts.statement: The species was formally named and described in 2018 by a team led by Xu Xing.
facts.quote: In 2018, Xu Xing, Paul Upchurch, Philip D. Mannion, Paul M. Barrett, Omar R. Regalado-Fernandez, Mo Jinyou, Ma Jinfu and Liu Hongan named and described the type species Lingwulong shenqi.

facts.statement: Unlike most other diplodocoids, Lingwulong possessed a U-shaped snout.
facts.quote: Unlike most other diplodocoids, which have square-shaped snouts in dorsal view, Lingwulong had a U-shaped snout.

facts.statement: Lingwulong was a respectable-sized sauropod reaching 17 meters in length, 4.5 meters in height, and weighing 15 tonnes.
facts.quote: Lingwulong fue un saurópodo de tamaño respetable, alcanzó los 17 metros de laro, 4,5 de alto y un peso de 15 toneladas.

facts.statement: Unique traits distinguishing Lingwulong include elaborate ornamentation along the upper orbital margin, a transversely wide occipital condyle, and anterior dorsal vertebrae with twisted metapophyses featuring a sub-circular pseudofacet.
facts.quote: Las autapomorfías, rasgos únicos, que distinguen a Lingwulong de otros diplodocoides incluyen una ornamentación muy elaborada a lo largo del margen superior del área orbital, cóndilo occipital con superficie articular transversalmente ancha y vértebras dorsal anterior con metapófisis ligeramente retorcidas que presentan un pseudofaceta subcircular en su punta.

facts.statement: Lingwulong lived during the early to middle Jurassic, approximately 178 to 168 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió entre principios a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 178 a 168 millones de años, desde el Toarciense al Bajociense, en lo que es hoy Asia

facts.statement: Research dating the Yanan Formation suggests Lingwulong lived between 174.0 and 171.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Subsequent research on the Yanan Formation dated it more precisely as Aalenian in age, largely between 174.0 and 171.7 Ma.

facts.statement: Some researchers argue the fossils came from the Zhiluo Formation, which would make Lingwulong younger, dating to the Bathonian to early Oxfordian.
facts.quote: However, the Lingwu dinosaur fauna has been argued to have actually come from the Zhiluo Formation, which would make Lingwulong substantially younger, Bathonian to early Oxfordian in age.

facts.statement: Lingwulong is one of the earliest known neosauropods and the only definitive diplodocoid found in East Asia.
facts.quote: It is one of the earliest neosauropods ever discovered, as well as the only definitive diplodocoid from east Asia.

facts.statement: Recent 2025 analyses suggest Lingwulong is a sister taxon to Cetiosauriscus, potentially outside the Flagellicaudata clade or within Diplodocidae.
facts.quote: In their 2025 phylogenetic analyses, Mannion and Moore recovered Lingwulong as a sister taxon of Cetiosauriscus, being either outside the clade Flagellicaudata, which contains the Diplodocidae and Dicraeosauridae, or within Diplodocidae.

facts.statement: The presence of Lingwulong challenges the East Asian Isolation Hypothesis, suggesting diplodocoids were present in East Asia during the Jurassic.
facts.quote: The discovery of Lingwulong casts doubt on these paleobiogeographical assumptions by showing that diplodocoids were present in East Asia during the Jurassic.

facts.statement: Lingwulong lived in China during the Early or Middle Jurassic period within the Yanan Formation.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en la Formación Yanan del Jurásico Temprano o Medio, de Lingwu, Yinchuan, Ningxia Hui, China.

facts.statement: It is the oldest known neosauropod and the only definitive diplodocoid found in East Asia.
facts.quote: Es el neosaurópodo más antiguo jamás descubierto, así como el único diplodocoide definitivo del este de Asia.

facts.statement: Its exact age is uncertain, but it lived between the late Toarcian and Bajocian, with an estimated midpoint age of 174 million years.
facts.quote: Su edad exacta es incierta, pero vivió entre los últimos años Toarciano y Bajociano, con una edad estimada de punto medio de 174 millones de años.

facts.statement: In 2004, sheep herder Ma Yun discovered dinosaur bones and notified local administrators Yang Huozhu and Liu Hongan.
facts.quote: En 2004, el pastor de ovejas Ma Yun encontró huesos de dinosaurios, notificando a los administradores locales Yang Huozhu y Liu Hongan.

facts.statement: Excavations at Ciyaopu near Lingwu from 2005 onwards revealed remains from about seven to ten sauropod skeletons.
facts.quote: Desde 2005 en adelante, varias canteras excavadas en Ciyaopu, cerca de Lingwu, en Ningxia Hui. Los restos fueron descubiertos de unos siete a diez esqueletos de saurópodos.

facts.statement: The species Lingwulong shenqi was named and described in 2018 by Xu Xing, Paul Upchurch, Philip D. Mannion, Paul M. Barrett, Omar R. Regalado-Fernández, Mo Jinyou, Ma Jinfu, and Liu Hongan.
facts.quote: En 2018, Xu Xing, Paul Upchurch, Philip D. Mannion, Paul M. Barrett, Omar R. Regalado-Fernández, Mo Jinyou, Ma Jinfu y Liu Hongan nombraron y describieron la especie tipo Lingwulong shenqi.

facts.statement: The generic name combines a reference to Lingwu with the Chinese word 'long' for dragon.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico combina una referencia a Lingwu con el long del mandarín , "dragón".

facts.statement: The specific name means 'amazing' in Mandarin, reflecting the unexpected appearance of a Dicraeosauridae member in East Asia, a group never before identified in the region.
facts.quote: El nombre específico significa "asombroso" en mandarín, lo que refleja la aparición inesperada de un miembro de Dicraeosauridae en el este de Asia, un grupo nunca antes identificado en la región.

facts.statement: The holotype LM V001a consists of the back of a skull associated with a series of teeth in their original position, dating to approximately 174 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo , LM V001a, se encontró en una capa de la Formación Yanan que data del Toarciano al Bajociano, de aproximadamente 174 millones de años. Consiste en la parte posterior de un cráneo asociado con una serie de dientes dentarios que se encuentran en su posición original.

facts.statement: The paratype LGP V001b is a partial skeleton lacking the skull, containing posterior back vertebrae, sacrum, pelvis, the first tail vertebra, and elements of the right hind limb.
facts.quote: El paratipo, LGP V001b, es un esqueleto parcial que carece del cráneo. Contiene las vértebras posteriores de la espalda, el sacro, la pelvis, la primera vértebra de la cola y elementos de la extremidad posterior derecha.

facts.statement: Specimen IVPP V23704 is a series of twenty-nine teeth.
facts.quote: IVPP V23704 es una serie de veintinueve dientes dentarios.

facts.statement: Specimen LGP V002 is a partial skeleton including back and tail vertebrae, the shoulder girdle, and elements of the forelimbs and pelvis.
facts.quote: LGP V002 es un esqueleto parcial que incluye vértebras de la espalda y la cola, la cintura escapular y elementos de las extremidades anteriores y la pelvis.

facts.statement: Specimen LGP V003 is a partial skeleton containing a series of vertebrae including dorsals, sacrals, the first two caudals, and both ilia.
facts.quote: LGP V003 es un esqueleto parcial que contiene una serie de vértebras que incluyen dorsales, sacros y los dos primeros caudales, y ambas ilions.

facts.statement: Specimen LGP V004 consists of a front neck vertebra, a rear front vertebra, and a right tibia from a small individual.
facts.quote: LGP V004 consta de una vértebra frontal del cuello, una vértebra frontal posterior y una tibia derecha de un individuo pequeño.

facts.statement: Specimen LGP V005 is a partial skeleton containing the sacrum, pelvis, and a series of twenty-five front and middle tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: LGP V005 es un esqueleto parcial que contiene el sacro, la pelvis y una serie de veinticinco vértebras de la cola delantera y media.

facts.statement: Lingwulong is included in the cladogram of Flagellicaudata as presented by Xu and colleagues in 2018.
facts.quote: El cladograma simplificado de Flagellicaudata con Lingwulong incluido en el, realizado por Xu y sus colegas (2018) se muestra a continuación:

facts.statement: The parent group of Lingwulong is Flagellicaudata.
facts.quote: Parent group: Flagellicaudata

facts.statement: Lingwulong belongs to the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: The time range for Lingwulong is from the Aalenian to the Callovian, between 174.7 and 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aalenian to Callovian (174.7 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether diplodocoids were absent from East Asia due to the Turgai Sea, a view supported by the 'East Asia Isolation Hypothesis' which explained the presence of mamenchisaurids in East Asia but not elsewhere.
facts.quote: Durante mucho tiempo se pensó que los diplodocoides habían estado ausentes en el este de Asia debido a la presencia del Mar de Turgai, y la 'Hipótesis de Aislamiento del Este de Asia' se usó para explicar la presencia de mamenquisáuridos en Asia Oriental pero no en otras partes del mundo.

facts.statement: The discovery of Lingwulong casts doubt on these paleobiogeographical assumptions by showing that diplodocoids were present in East Asia in the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de Lingwulong arroja dudas sobre estas suposiciones paleobiogeográficas al mostrar que los diplodocoides estaban presentes en el este de Asia a principios del Jurásico.
